objectives: Students will be able to understand and describe the systems engineering concepts.
Students will be able to introduce systems engineering as a problem solving approach.
Students will be able to understand the systems engineering methods and tools.
Students will be able to understand various systems engineering concepts through a course project.
Students will be able to write an effective systems design written report and oral presentation.
topics: Introduction to Systems Engineering and Systems Engineering Design Thinking concepts Integrated Product and Subsystems I

objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to use the techniques that form the basis for the numerical modeling of fluid systems.
By the end of this course, students will be able to apply fundamental engineering concepts to airfoil/wing design.
By the end of this course, students will be able to calculate and/or model aerodynamic forces and moments any flight vehicle at any speed and any aerodynamic attitude.
By the end of this course, students will be able to use Mach number, Reynolds number, and the principle of dynamic similarity and their key influences in the field of wind tunnel testing.
By the end of this course, students will be able to communicate and interpret the results of their wind tunnel testing.

objectives: Students will be able to understand and describe the aerospace structures and materials.
Students will be able to understand and know the various loads on aerospace structures and their analysis.
Students will be able to understand the linear elasticity and thin-walled sections.
Students will be able to understand various materials and manufacturing used for aerospace structures.
Students will be able to evaluate the aerospace structural performance and durability related to safety.
topics: Introduction to Aerospace Structures and Materials Aircraft Loads Linear Elasticity Torsion, Bending, and Flexural Shear
